newsitem.title: Australia: SFE wheat pauses, holds against Chicago fall.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat pauses, holds against Chicago fall.

text.p: Australian wheat futures traded lower in subdued fashion on Wednesday, resisting the full extent of Chicago's overnight fall.
January 1997 fell A$1.50 to A$143.50 a tonne and March 1997 fell A$2.00 to A$145.00 in eight lots each in Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) floor trading.
This followed Tuesday's record SFE volume of 261 trades, including SFE floor trading and SYCOM trading the night before.
Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures Ltd said SFE wheat futures prices surprised by staying so high.

Chicago's overnight fall of 11 cents to US$3.68-3/4 a bushel for December futures and Argentina's aggressive undercutting of Australia on world markets created conditions for a greater price decline, he said.

"I'd say the current prices we're seeing in Australian Standard White futures are probably substantially higher than what they should be," he said. "They provide excellent opportunities for growers and speculators alike to sell."
Ord Minnett chartists were looking at A$130.00 a tonne for January 1997 futures, he said.
"Prices have come off so much and there's so much aggressive selling on world markets that prices will probably stay sluggish for some time yet," he said.
Rain affecting the current New South Wales harvest would dominate the local market, Lindsay said.
